message.content: In lions, one of the most striking dominant traits is the development of the mane in adult male lions. The presence of a mane is controlled by a dominant allele (often referred to as **M**), while the absence of a mane (as seen in females and younger males) is due to the recessive allele (**m**). Thus, when a male lion inherits at least one copy of the dominant **M** allele from either parent, it will develop a mane.
